title: Majestic Bishop
summary: Choose the promotion that keeps Black moving, then coordinate bishop and knight for mate.

nodes.question: Which promotion avoids the stalemate defense?
nodes.explanation: White has Ka6, Nc5 and c6 against Ka8 and Ba7. The knight controls b7, while the king controls a7 and b7. Black can use ...Bb8 to make major-piece promotion stalemate.

branches.title: Promote to a bishop and close the cage
commentary: Begin from the complete five-piece source board. The defender’s dark-square bishop is essential to the promotion choices.
c7 advances toward promotion without changing the knight’s control of b7.
Bb8 offers the bishop while setting a stalemate trap against queen or rook promotion.
c8=B promotes to a light-square bishop, leaving the black bishop free to move.
Bf4 is the illustrated retreat. The dark-square bishop cannot capture White’s pieces on light squares.
Nd7 controls b8 and leaves the black king without a safe king move, preparing Bb7 mate.
Be3 is the source’s selected bishop move; it cannot stop the light-square mating attack.
Bb7# is actual mate. Ka6 protects b7 and covers a7, while Nd7 covers b8.
branches.explanation: Bb7# is actual mate. Ka6 protects b7 and covers a7, while Nd7 covers b8.

branches.title: Promote to a queen
commentary: Compare the source’s natural queen promotion against ...Bb8.
c7 keeps White’s exact win until the promotion choice.
Bb8 sets the pin-and-stalemate defense.
c8=Q is actual stalemate: Bb8 is pinned to Ka8, b7 is controlled by Nc5 and Ka6, and a7 is covered by Ka6.
branches.explanation: c8=Q is actual stalemate: Bb8 is pinned to Ka8, b7 is controlled by Nc5 and Ka6, and a7 is covered by Ka6.

branches.title: Promote to a rook
commentary: The rook has the same stalemating horizontal pin as the queen.
c7 advances the pawn while retaining the win.
Bb8 prepares to be pinned across the eighth rank.
c8=R is actual stalemate. The pinned bishop cannot move and Ka8 has no legal flight square.
branches.explanation: c8=R is actual stalemate. The pinned bishop cannot move and Ka8 has no legal flight square.

branches.title: Capture the offered bishop
commentary: Compare capturing the bishop instead of promoting straight ahead.
c7 advances the pawn toward promotion.
Bb8 offers the bishop beside its king.
cxb8=Q+ exchanges the pawn for the bishop, but the new queen is not protected.
Kxb8 captures the queen. White has only king and knight against king, an exact draw.
branches.explanation: Kxb8 captures the queen. White has only king and knight against king, an exact draw.

branches.title: Try a second knight
commentary: Compare the source’s knight promotion and the illustrated king escape.
c7 prepares promotion.
Bb8 offers the same defensive setup.
c8=N avoids immediate stalemate, but does not preserve a forced win.
Bf4 is the illustrated retreat, leaving White without the bishop mating diagonal.
Nb6+ gives check with the newly promoted knight.
Kb8 escapes along the eighth rank.
Ncd7+ checks with the original c5 knight, but does not form the bishop-and-knight mating cage.
Kc7 is the illustrated escape. The exact position remains drawn despite White’s extra knight.
branches.explanation: Kc7 is the illustrated escape. The exact position remains drawn despite White’s extra knight.

exercises.prompt: Why does promotion to a weaker piece help?
exercises.answer: A queen or rook pins Bb8 and leaves Black no legal move. A bishop leaves the dark-square bishop mobile while supplying the light-square Bb7 mating diagonal.
The knight controls b8 and the king controls a7/b7. Black must move its bishop, which cannot stop Bb7 on a light square.

startContext: The complete five-piece source root is visually reconstructed. Selected source comparisons cover all four straight promotion choices and capturing the offered bishop. The successful light-square bishop promotion reaches actual mate, while queen/rook promotion stalemate and knight promotion draws. Every encoded position is checked exactly.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
